title: Voice, Vision, and the End of Text-Only AI
summary: Modern AI models can see images, hear speech, and talk back. Here's what multimodal actually means, what today's flagship models can do as of 2026-08-02, and which features matter for everyday use.
before: AI assistants processed text only. To work with images or audio, you needed separate tools and manual conversion steps.
after: Flagship models handle text, images, audio, and video in a single conversation. No switching tools or converting files.

title: Before You Trust an AI Agent With Your Accounts
summary: AI agents can now manage your email, calendar, and finances. But the same features that make them useful also make them risky. Here is what to check before granting access.
before: Could only read and respond. The worst outcome was a bad answer or embarrassing output.
after: Can read, write, and act across connected accounts. A mistake or attack can move money, delete data, or send messages.

title: AI That Uses Your Computer: What Screen-Control Agents Can and Cannot Do
summary: Computer-use agents can now click, type, and navigate your screen. Here is what they actually automate today, where they fail, and what to check before giving one your credentials.
before: You describe a task in words, and the AI gives you instructions to follow yourself. The AI never touches your screen.
after: You describe a task, and the agent sees your screen, moves the mouse, types, and completes the workflow autonomously.

title: What AI Agents Actually Do in 2026
summary: AI agents have moved beyond chatbot territory. Here is what they actually do now, how they connect to your tools, and why MCP became the standard.
before: You ask a question, get an answer. No memory between sessions, no ability to take actions or access outside systems.
after: The AI plans multi-step tasks, uses tools, reads from databases, and takes actions in connected apps - with your approval.

title: Open Source AI Models Are Closing the Gap
summary: Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, and Qwen have gone from distant followers to genuine contenders. Here's what that shift actually means.
before: Open source models lagged 12-18 months behind GPT-4. Running them required serious hardware and expertise.
after: Top open models trade blows with the closed frontier on many benchmarks. Some run efficiently on consumer hardware.

title: Why Every Lab Is Racing to Build Coding Agents
summary: Coding assistants used to suggest the next line. Now they open pull requests. Here's why AI labs see autonomous coding as the killer app.
before: AI suggests code snippets as you type. You review each suggestion, accept or reject, and do the actual work of building features.
after: AI reads your issue, writes the code, runs tests, and opens a pull request. You review the finished work, not individual suggestions.
